correctness.rationale: The canonical walks through 0 distinguish neither starting point nor orientation, and a connected disjoint pair of perfect matchings gives exactly an undirected Hamilton cycle. The symmetric difference for a two-edge move is a nonempty even subgraph with four edges in a simple graph of girth four; a four-cycle of the cube alternates two axes and is a face. Adjacent removed face edges would change a vertex degree by two, so the removed edges are opposite. Thus the face test with Hamiltonicity and the cycle-pair symmetric-difference test enumerate exactly the requested adjacency. The whole cube automorphism group is accounted for: after a translation an automorphism fixes 0, a coordinate permutation accounts for its permutation of the neighbors of 0, and distances to 0 and the four unit vectors determine every vertex. The separate full enumeration reproduced 1344 cycles (also from 272 perfect matchings), all 24 faces, 1920 edges, degree counts (240,384,192,288,240) at (0,1,2,4,8), components 1^240 and 1104, radius 10 and diameter 12, eccentricity counts (96,192,816), all nine orbit-size/degree pairs, and all twelve unordered pair-distance counts, with total 608856.
residual_risks: The enumeration is exhaustive only for the defined graph on Q₄ and the specified moves; it is not a higher-dimensional result or a formal proof certificate.

evidence: The dense-graph theorem uses switches of size up to 10 and minimum degree at least n/2+7. The 2018 study covers inversions across dimensions and reports three of nine isolated types in dimension four. The later Resultary theorem covers the same graph and gives a further orbit-neighbor table.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither the dense-graph sufficient condition (4<15 here) nor a count of isolated types implies that the remaining labeled cycles form one component or gives its distances. The later record overlaps at the required parameters and on the very same state model.

value.rationale: The Hamilton-cycle move graph is a natural reconfiguration and constrained-sampling object. The precise decomposition distinguishes immobile cycles from a single freely connected class, and the distances quantify the number of moves required within that class. Orbit-degree data identify how this structure depends on symmetry type. This is a complete labeled metric census, not a re-tabulation of the known state count or the known count of isolated types.
residual_risks: No mixing-time guarantee follows from the census; higher dimensions and larger switches are not classified.
